Jito paid by pull, not push. Its open-source distributor (GPL-3.0) is a program that distributes tokens from an uploaded Merkle root and can pay a mix of unlocked and linearly unlocking tokens. Claimants use a web page or a Rust CLI; the CLI creates the claimant's associated token account if it does not exist. Validators sign claims with their identity keypair through the CLI, which Jito says preserves key-management best practice; the JTO lands in a token account owned by that identity before the validator moves it to another wallet.

On Solana a push airdrop needs one token account per new holder, about 0.002 SOL of rent each plus a ~0.000005 SOL base fee, so cost scales with recipient count. Helius, which sells the tool, says ZK-compressed distribution cuts a 10,000-recipient airdrop from about 20 SOL to about 0.01 SOL. A merkle claim model such as Jito's pushes the account-creation step to the claimant.

SlowMist reported a 2025 case (coverage dated 2025-12-03 to 2025-12-05) in which a victim signed a transaction containing the assign instruction and lost control of the wallet: the signing preview showed no asset change, later transfer and revoke attempts from the account failed, and over $3 million was stolen with more funds temporarily locked in DeFi protocols. SlowMist compares it to the 'malicious multisig' attacks seen on TRON and lists it among four representative 2025 phishing patterns. All three sources trace to SlowMist's own advisory and report, so this is one origin.

Some Solana drainers defeat transaction simulation (time of check to time of use, TOCTOU). The wallet simulates a benign result. After the user signs, the attacker's server changes on-chain state that the malicious program reads, then submits the signed transaction, which now drains. In Blockaid's Vanish Drainer example the state flag was the existence of a token account for one specific mint. The state-setting transaction landed at block 247363970 and the drain seven blocks later (about $3,000 lost). Blockaid said in January 2024 that Solana drainers can deceive wallet simulations, and Blowfi

Jupiter Shield shows swap-time warnings: Not Verified, Low Organic Activity, New Listing, Has Freeze Authority and Has Mint Authority. In September 2024 Cointelegraph reported that Jupiter and RugCheck had built indicators for tokens that enable the Permanent Delegate extension. Jupiter states its indicators are informational and 'not guarantees of safety'. The list of warnings changes over time.

Each project sets its own definition of 'sybil', and it can cover usage the project itself promoted. LayerZero labelled the Merkly bridge a 'Sybil farming application' although it lists Merkly in its own ecosystem. Critics warned that active users could be mislabelled and that the approach would disqualify genuine low-net-worth users with 1 to 3 wallets; those critics are airdrop farmers or Merkly's adviser, so they are not neutral. LayerZero's founder replied 'If you are a real user doing real things, you should be fine.'

The spl-token CLI covers each step for accounts you own: 'spl-token burn' burns tokens from an account, 'spl-token close --address <TOKEN_ACCOUNT>' closes one account (recipient defaults to the owner), and 'spl-token gc --close-empty-associated-accounts' closes all empty associated token accounts to recover SOL. The CLI accepts --program-2022 or --program-id to target Token-2022 accounts. The catch is signing: unless a Ledger is used, Sol Incinerator says the CLI needs the wallet's keypair or recovery phrase, which for a browser wallet means exporting its secret.

Phantom says only Actions and Blinks registered in the Dialect-maintained registry unfurl in the X feed and that Phantom renders only registered ones; unverified Blinks show as ordinary URLs. The same page says the wallet simulates a Blink transaction before approval and that Phantom's X support is opt-in, disabled by default as of June 2024. This is Phantom's description of its own design; no independent evaluation was found.

zkSync's June 2024 airdrop shows both ends of the strictness dial. Critics said it had 'almost no Sybil filtering' (Polygon's security chief Mudit Gupta) and 'no anti-Sybil program' (Adam Cochran). Researcher Ignas pointed to zkSync's own statement that 'Sybil detection often cuts out real users with arbitrary filters', and a sybil tracker's preliminary estimate was 135 million ZK going to wallets on LayerZero's sybil list. zkSync's documentation instead describes a deliberately conservative step that removed clusters of more than 20 EOAs sharing an ultimate funder or CEX deposit address (one

zkSync's June 2024 airdrop shows the strictness dial in public. Mudit Gupta of Polygon said it had 'almost no Sybil filtering' and Adam Cochran said it 'had no anti-Sybil program'. A researcher pointed to zkSync's own line that 'Sybil detection often cuts out real users with arbitrary filters', and a sybil tracker's preliminary estimate put 135 million ZK on wallets that LayerZero had listed as sybils. The ZK Nation documentation says eligibility rules, value scaling and multipliers removed most bot swarms and that a 'very conservative' final step filtered every cluster above 20 externally own

Design remedies recur across independent sources: scale rewards to costs users actually bear (low fees make transaction-count thresholds cheap), run several rounds and tighten criteria between them, weight by time and amount, require multi-step activity, and add vesting or extra steps for large payouts. Jupiter's January 2025 rules applied several: a $5 per-transaction floor, discounts for stablecoin and SOL-to-SOL swaps, an 8-of-12-month consistency bonus and time-weighted stake.

Locks and vesting are widely recommended but untested as an airdrop design. The arXiv airdrop study leaves 'lockdrops' to future work. Streamflow, a vesting vendor, says vested airdrops outperform but its Solana Airdrop Quality Index has no formula or scores. Blocksmith proposes time, milestone and KPI vesting and options airdrops. Solana practice mixes partial vesting (Jito's 12-month linear unlock for validators and searchers), delayed-claim bonuses (Drift) and staking bonuses (Jupiter Carrots).

Flat per-wallet payouts made cheap multi-wallet farms very profitable on Solana. Jupiter's first airdrop gave every eligible wallet (about 955,000) a flat 200 JUP regardless of volume. Jupiter Research and Allium (2024-02-27) found one attacker whose 10,613 wallets claimed nearly 2M JUP with swaps under one cent each. Lookonchain, reported by crypto.news (2024-02-01), traced a 9,246-wallet farmer that claimed 1.85M JUP, which is 200 JUP per wallet (derived), and sold 1.4M JUP ($898K) at $0.6371. At that price each wallet returned about $127 (derived: 200 times $0.6371). Neither source reports

One Solana transaction can hold many instructions, so one signature can drain SOL and several token balances at once (STMT). SolPhishHunter's example drain carries five transfer instructions: four token types plus SOL. Raydium warns that the transfer to the scammer is often buried among harmless instructions, and advises rejecting any prompt with more than 3 to 4 instructions from programs you do not recognise.

Jupiter forum threads (Solana) show naive sybil proxies being proposed and challenged by users. In July 2024 one user proposed excluding wallets staking 1 JUP or less from the next airdrop after wallets staking under 0.1 JUP rose from 29,157 to 36,302 in 12 days. Replies said correlation is not causation, that the small stakes might be dust left after unstaking, and that some whales use several wallets for security; the proposer suggested a minimum cumulative vote count so such wallets 'don't get labelled incorrectly'. In October 2024 other posters said 'Everyone I know has more than 1 wallet'

Published filter criteria get turned into farming advice. A Substack post that paraphrases Wormhole's disclosure, by an author who says they have 'a vested interest that Zenith does well' (a farming-automation tool), advises clusters of 5 wallets or fewer, randomised CEX withdrawal amounts and times, and avoiding bursts of small identical transfers. The post adds no independent check of Wormhole's methods.

Funding-graph heuristics overcount sybils unless exchange hubs are removed first. Liu and Zhu note that many accounts receive funds from CEX hot wallets, forming perfect star patterns, and that ordinary accounts 'might be tagged as Sybil's account by mistake'. A small HackMD analysis of Mantle and BSC airdrop lists found 13 of 16 BSC star hubs were exchange wallets. Removing them cut members of clusters of 10 or more from 218 to 56 on BSC and from 217 to 142 on Mantle. The author states the result 'does not confirm malicious intent on its own'.

BlockEden's account of the planned final round: 170M JUP to fee-paying users (swaps, perps, lending) and 30M JUP to stakers, a snapshot closing 2026-01-30, a 200M JUP bonus pool for people who hold and stake what they receive, and staker rates of 0.1 JUP per staked JUP plus 0.3 for Super Voters who voted in 13 of 17 proposals. Only this one outlet gave the split; Jupiter's support page for the criteria needs a login and could not be read.

Push airdrops on Solana cost about 0.002 SOL per new recipient for the associated token account plus 0.000005 SOL in fees, so 10,000 recipients cost about 20 SOL with new accounts, about 0.05 SOL if recipients already hold accounts, and about 0.01 SOL with ZK-compressed tokens, according to Helius, a vendor that sells compression.

The Solana runtime lets only an account's owner program debit its lamports or change its data, and only the current owner can reassign the owner (the account must be writable and its data zeroed). A wallet account starts out owned by the System Program, so a victim who signs a transaction containing the System Program assign instruction hands the wallet's owner field to attacker-chosen code. The SolPhish paper calls this Account Authority Transfer (AAT) and pairs it with SetAuthority of type 'account owner', which makes the phisher the owner of a token account. SlowMist's 2025 report documents

Fake clones of the Sol Incinerator cleanup site exist (PCrisk documents sol-incinerator[.]tax, updated 2026-01-14). They promise rewards for burning tokens, are promoted through fake social accounts and ads, and activate a wallet drainer on connect. The real tool says each transaction is approved in your own wallet and that a recovery phrase or private key must never be entered into a cleanup site.

Forum advice mostly says to ignore or hide an unsolicited transfer and not to interact with it, but it carries errors. In two Reddit mirror snapshots (one about ETH dust, one about a token in Ledger Wallet) the dominant replies are to hide or ignore it; one reply says sending a token to another wallet 'infects' it, with no evidence; the single reply advising burn-and-reclaim-rent on Solana scored 0 points. Neither thread is about Solana token accounts specifically, so treat them as sentiment, not evidence.

One cleanup-tool author (Jumpbit, self-reported and promotional) says closing 897 empty token accounts across 50 airdrop-farming wallets recovered 1.83 SOL in under three minutes, and that burning 37 spam token accounts recovered about 0.075 SOL, which he describes as the rent the spammers had paid. The figures match the pre-2026 rent of about 0.002 SOL per account but are not an independent measurement of how many spam accounts a typical wallet holds.

Farming tooling lowers per-wallet cost, the discount factor in TierDrop's model. Kerman Kohli (2023-10-19) describes dashboards that run wallet groups with randomised timing and random actions, track expenses per wallet, and auto-consolidate and withdraw to a CEX, plus airdrop simulators that score wallets against past criteria (one zkSync table had 765,000 rows). The Block (2023-04-06) reports a farming team trialling software that randomises transaction amounts and frequency, while another farmer does everything manually.

The Permissioned Burn extension lets an issuer take burning away from holders. Once a burn authority is set on the mint, the regular Burn and BurnChecked instructions are rejected (process_burn returns InvalidInstruction) and every burn needs the issuer's burn authority as a co-signer; setting the authority to None re-enables ordinary burns. A spam mint using it would leave the holder unable to burn, and so unable to close. The extension appears in the main-branch Token-2022 docs and source (program crate version 12.0.0 at the time of reading); whether the deployed mainnet binary includes it w

The spl-token CLI covers the manual route. 'spl-token burn <ACCOUNT> ALL' burns the whole balance and 'spl-token close --address <ACCOUNT>' closes an account; add --program-2022 for Token-2022 accounts. 'spl-token gc --close-empty-associated-accounts' (help text: close all empty associated token accounts, to get SOL back) is not a spam cleaner: in its code it never closes an associated account while any account for that mint carries a balance, skips frozen accounts, skips empty accounts that have a separate close authority (it prints a note to rerun with --owner), and for a non-associated acco

Mandiant published a YARA rule for hunting CLINKSINK pages that matches solanaWeb3 call names (Connection, SystemProgram.transfer, findProgramAddress), helper function names such as createTxs, claimSolana and createTokenTxs, Phantom detection strings and SPL token instruction names, and warns that it needs validation against an organisation's own data before it informs any blocking.

After an owner reassignment the victim could not transfer funds, revoke authorizations or use DeFi positions. In SlowMist's December 2025 case more than $3 million was stolen and about $2 million held in DeFi protocols could not be moved. ChainCatcher reports that about $2 million was rescued with the protocols' help. SlowMist advises checking every signature for hidden Owner changes before approving.

Public Solana drain losses are small next to EVM and depend on the counting method. ScamSniffer attributed about $4.17 million and 3,947 victims to two drainers in early 2024 (Rainbow about $2.14 million and 2,189 victims; Node about $2.02 million and 1,759 victims in under two weeks). SolPhishHunter's three Solana-specific transaction types found 8,058 phishing transactions and about $1.10 million of loss. SlowMist's 2025 incident archive ranks Solana third at about $17.45 million, but that archive excludes individual user losses.

Projects treat a person's several wallets in three different ways. Wormhole builds an ownership graph that gives one user ID to a wallet cluster, tests the minimum cumulative transfer value (median about $1,500 after adjustments) across all linked wallets, and spreads the reward over all of them; its FAQ admits this lets wallets with one small transaction qualify. Jupiter allocates per wallet: linking wallets in a Jupiverse Profile 'will have no effect whatsoever' on the allocation and scores are not summed. Arbitrum and ZKsync remove clusters above a size cutoff: Arbitrum lists 'a cluster of

Jito excluded all past and current core contributors, including core-contributor wallets holding JitoSOL, validators they operate and canary searchers they operate. Recipients had 18 months from the token generation date to claim; after that, unclaimed JTO moves permissionlessly to the DAO treasury's Realms wallet.

Drainers defeat wallet transaction previews in at least three documented ways: anti-simulation techniques and fake simulation results (victims confirmed even after a 'simulation failed' message), bit-flip drainers (Aqua, Vanish) that change on-chain data after signing, and TOCTOU programs whose malicious branch is inactive during simulation and activated by a state-changing transaction the attacker sends after the user signs.

Wallet and DEX safety guides rank airdrop bait among the main Solana scam types. Raydium sorts most losses into five buckets (seed-phrase theft, phishing dApps, fake tokens, airdrop bait, social engineering) and treats rug pulls as a separate token-selection problem; Phantom's list leads with fake giveaways and airdrops delivered through spam NFTs or ads.

Lures are tailored to the holders and communities of popular Solana tokens. Wallet Guard flagged a drainer kit aimed at Bonk, Jupiter, Chonky, Galactic Geckos and dogwifhat communities (2023-12-29); Scam Sniffer tied Rainbow Drainer to phishing NFTs airdropped to ZERO holders and Node Drainer to a Christmas campaign aimed at Bonk holders; Mandiant saw BONK-themed pages.

Lures that copy live Solana airdrops were still circulating in 2026. PCRisk documented a fake 'Solana Seeker ($SKR) Airdrop' site (updated 2026-01-28) where connecting a wallet signs a malicious contract that feeds a drainer, and ThreatCluster (2026-05-22, citing SolanaFloor and ChainCatcher monitoring) reported fake CJUP tokens airdropped into wallets to impersonate Jupiter and push holders to phishing sites. Neither source gives victim counts or losses.

A normal Solana transaction expires after about 150 blocks (roughly 80 to 90 seconds). A durable nonce removes that expiry: the transaction's first instruction advances a nonce account, and a signed transaction stays valid until the nonce changes. A signature can therefore be held and submitted later. SolPhishHunter found 14 multi-transfer drain transactions that used advanceNonce, and says this lets phishers delay execution so the loss and the detection come later.

Token Extension Program ATAs created through the Associated Token Program get ImmutableOwner automatically, so SetAuthority on their owner fails with TokenError::ImmutableOwner. The classic Token program has no such protection: its InitializeImmutableOwner only logs 'Please upgrade to SPL Token 2022 for immutable owner support', and its SetAuthority path has no immutable-owner check.

Hiding is display-only; burning and closing change on-chain state. Data Clinic says hiding removes a token from view 'without deleting it from the blockchain'. MadeOnSol presents hiding in Phantom and Solflare as 'a display control, not a security measure'. Phantom's report action hides the asset and also feeds Phantom's spam detection.

Wallet, DEX and protocol guidance agrees that receiving an unsolicited token is not a compromise, and that the default response is to hide or report it and leave it alone. Phantom: receiving an unfamiliar asset does not mean the wallet is compromised; report it as spam to hide it. Solflare: the mere presence of a token in the wallet does not pose an inherent threat. Data Clinic: simply receiving the tokens does not mean the wallet is compromised; hide it and ignore it. Raydium: ignore unknown tokens and turn on the wallet's hide-unknown-tokens setting. Cielo: separate suspicious tokens from yo

Self-reported farmer economics are scale-driven and selectively reported. Farmers described using about 100 wallets for one airdrop; one reported $15,000 from Arbitrum against roughly $1,000 of transaction fees on about $300,000 of volume; a team claimed close to $1 million total, though its itemised amounts sum to about $725,000. Figures are pseudonymous, unverified, priced at launch, and drawn from successes.

Academic work on Solana phishing (SolPhishHunter, arXiv May 2025) names Account Authority Transfer as one of three Solana-specific phishing transaction types. Phishers use Assign to set a wallet account's owner to a malicious program, and SetAuthority(account owner) to take token accounts. The paper contrasts this with Ethereum, where approval and transfer are separate steps, and says it is more likely to deceive new users.

Wallet simulation can be defeated, so a clean preview of an Approve or authority change is not proof of safety. In the Bull Checker case the extension replaced the wallet adapter's signTransaction, kept the simulated SOL balance at zero so malicious instructions stayed dormant, and then bundled the drain after simulation. A drainer guide also warns that a delegate approval looks like a routine SPL token program call in the preview.

Solana Actions and Blinks put a transaction request behind a link in a social post. Phantom says its support on X is off by default, the wallet simulates the transaction first, and at launch only Blinks registered in the Dialect-maintained registry unfurl on X (unregistered ones show as plain URLs); wallets may use another registry. The Solana Foundation said using Actions is like connecting a wallet to a dapp, so users should stick to trusted sites. I found no documented large Blink-based drainer campaign.

Most large airdrops pair automated filters with a human recourse path: Linea published a webpage to check sybil status and let flagged users appeal; Wormhole accepted reconsideration requests through a form and said cohorts would be reassessed and rewards were 'subject to change'; LayerZero reported about 30,000 appeals within the first hours of its bounty phase.

Large airdrops pair automated filters with a human recourse path. Linea published a web page to check sybil status and let flagged users appeal. Wormhole took reconsideration requests through a form. LayerZero reported about 30,000 appeals within hours of opening its bounty stage. Binance's BAB airdrop reclaimed rewards from suspected sybil addresses and ran a manual appeal review before treating them as confirmed.

Solana example of cheap wallet-scale farming being caught: Allium and Jupiter Research reported a 10,613-wallet botnet that claimed nearly 2M JUP in the Jupiter airdrop; its swaps were each under one cent in volume, its first swaps began as early as May 2023, and irregular timing and patterns gave it away (report dated 2024-02-27). Funding cost is not stated.

Ownership-transfer phishing is documented by three independent parties. SolPhishHunter (academic, May 2025) describes Assign on wallet accounts and SetAuthority on token accounts. GoPlus (January 2024) reports phishing sites that embed createSetAuthorityInstruction. Jupiter's August 2024 alert describes a victim who 'lost control of his tokenAuthority' to an attacker address.

Drainer operators instrument and filter the funnel. CLINKSINK pages call an attacker server that looks up the connecting wallet and balance, returns 'null' if the same wallet connects twice, and supplies config with minimum-value thresholds and a canned 'wallet is not eligible' message. ScamSniffer saw a Rainbow Drainer operator run a self-hosted Matomo instance to track each step and improve conversion. Low-value wallets can therefore be turned away while high-value wallets are drained.

Projects use points before a token exists to steer user behaviour. Rewarded actions seen on Solana include trading volume and PnL, lending and borrowing, liquidity provision, referrals, asset boosts, and not listing NFTs on rival marketplaces. Points need no fixed emissions schedule, so the team can retune rates between seasons.

Jupiter scored each wallet separately and did not sum linked wallets; Jupiverse Profiles only show allocations in one dashboard. A January 2026 forum post reports this fragments eligibility for users who migrated to the Jupiter Wallet, that the checker returned inconsistent states ('0', 'not eligible', blank) for one wallet, and that balances could be visible but not yet claimable behind a stake-gated step. It is one user's report and does not say which round it covers.

The much-quoted 2025 phishing drop (losses from $494M to $83.85M, victims from 332,000 to 106,106) covers EVM-compatible chains only. Scam Sniffer's methodology states 'Scope: EVM-compatible chains', wallet-drainer phishing sites only, USD value at time of theft, and a lower-bound estimate, and SlowMist's report repeats that scope for its drainer section. ForkLog's headline presents the same figure as 'Crypto Phishing Losses' without the scope. SlowMist's separate Solana figure of about $17.45M comes from its incident archive, which excludes individual user losses, so none of these is a 2025 S

For clawed-back airdrops, TokenTax says: if the project cut the allocation before the holder could move the tokens, nothing is reported and a filed return is corrected. If the holder had control and later returned the tokens, a return of more than $3,000 in a later year uses the claim-of-right rules in IRC section 1341, and $3,000 or less is deductible only by business filers. The IRS denied a section 165 loss in CCA 202302011 where the taxpayer had not abandoned or disposed of the tokens. TokenTax notes the IRS has issued no guidance on sybil clawbacks.

TokenTax advises on clawbacks as follows. If a project cut an allocation before the holder could move or sell tokens, nothing was received and the fix is an amended return, not a deduction. If the holder controlled the tokens and later returned them, more than $3,000 in a later year falls under the section 1341 claim-of-right rules, and $3,000 or less is deducted where the income was reported, which helps a business filer and not a hobby filer. TokenTax says the IRS has issued no guidance on sybil clawbacks.

CloseAccount needs a zero balance on non-native accounts and deletes the account, so any delegate stored on it is removed with it. The close authority signs, or the owner if no close authority is set. For an empty spam token account, closing clears a stale delegate and returns the rent deposit.

Anyone can create the associated token account (ATA) for any wallet and deposit tokens into it, so unsolicited tokens need no consent from the holder. In the ATA program's Create instruction the funding account is the only signer and the wallet address is a read-only non-signer. The program charges the funder for the new account (create_pda_account with the funder), and the wallet owns the account regardless of who created it.

At scale the amounts are small per account. A vendor-affiliated first-person post reports 897 empty token accounts across 50 wallets returning 1.83 SOL, and 118 accounts in one wallet returning 0.24 SOL, about 0.002 SOL per account and consistent with the rent figure; MadeOnSol gives approximately 0.00203 SOL per standard token account. No independent measurement of spam-account counts or recovered totals was found.

SolPhish's 'Impersonation of System Accounts' (ISA) class uses vanity addresses with matching prefixes or suffixes (e.g. '1111' suffix) to mimic official system accounts, exploiting wallets that show truncated addresses; it has no direct Ethereum counterpart in the paper.

Solana drainers are sold as a service. Mandiant tied at least 35 CLINKSINK affiliate IDs and 42 Solana wallet addresses to one drainer-as-a-service: the operator supplies the drainer script and keeps a share of stolen funds. CertiK found Solana drainer kits for sale from about $250 a month and said providers take a cut of stolen assets, as on EVM.

Phantom states it automatically hides all fungible tokens that have a URL in the name, auto-detects and hides spam NFTs, and hides anything users report as spam, using third-party verifications, machine learning, SimpleHash spam scores and user feedback. Phantom also treats words like 'Free', 'Gift', 'Limited' and 'Airdrop' in metadata as red flags.

Claim sites reach victims through several channels: hijacked official social accounts (Mandiant's own X account was hijacked on 2024-01-03 to push a CLINKSINK drainer link), X and Discord posts, and paid social or search ads that place a clone site above the real one.

Attackers reach victims through hijacked official accounts, ads, chat and DMs. Mandiant's own X account was taken over on 3 January 2024 to post a CLINKSINK link. Phantom lists hacked brand accounts, scam social ads, paid Google ads, Discord and Telegram DMs, and fake Telegram 'Safeguard' bots that make the victim run a command. Raydium warns that attackers buy Google ads for brand terms and register domains with lookalike characters.

Pre-filtering known non-user entities before clustering is standard practice: Arbitrum removes bridges, exchanges, smart contracts and CEX deposit addresses (using Nansen, Hop and OffChain Labs data) plus some manual removals, and Wormhole manually labelled contracts, protocol relayer hot wallets and large sybil clusters of hundreds to thousands of wallets.

A Linea community-forum post (3 March 2025) says wallets of honest users of the AdsPower multi-account browser were blocklisted after an AdsPower hack, that these users got no appeal route, and that 'after reviewing the appeals, an additional 13,586 addresses were added to the blocklist'. The author is a community member, not Linea staff, and the figure is unattributed. A commenter who manages four DeFi wallets through AdsPower calls the flag unfair; another commenter claims the affected wallets were sybil farms.

Vendors describe delegate-approval phishing on Solana. GoPlus (January 2024) says attackers hide createApproveCheckedInstruction behind fake voting or staking pages, so no assets move at signing and the attacker can withdraw later. Solana Compass and MadeOnSol describe the same pattern: an Approve hidden in a mint, claim or connect transaction and used hours or weeks later. None of the three gives an incident-level case or a loss figure.

Being flagged in an earlier airdrop is treated as a propensity signal, not proof. Allium says a flag from another airdrop earned extra scrutiny for Drift, not automatic exclusion. Artemis, by contrast, trains its ML model by labelling addresses excluded from past airdrops as sybil, and concedes those addresses 'might not have been sybils but could have just been low-engaged users'.

The subgraph-based LightGBM paper reports precision 0.9428, recall 0.9182, F1 0.9303 and AUC 0.9806 on a Binance Account Bound (BAB) airdrop dataset on BNB Smart Chain (193,701 addresses, 23,240 labelled sybil, 75 features from a two-hop transaction subgraph). It is tested on one airdrop dataset and compares against Trusta's clustering approach (precision 0.7962, recall 0.8159), so the figures are not evidence of performance on Solana.

Closing an emptied token account deletes its delegate state with it. Neither program's CloseAccount checks the delegate: a non-native account needs a zero balance and a signature from the close authority (or the owner). This is inferred from the source, not stated in the docs.
Linea's pre-airdrop filter (with Nansen) flagged about 516,960 of 1,297,203 eligible addresses as sybil, leaving 780,243, based on 'automated and coordinated activities across related wallets'.

Points programs are off-chain tallies kept by the issuer. The issuer alone sets the earning criteria, may change them between seasons, may hide accrued totals until a season ends, and often discloses how points convert to rewards only after distribution.

Three Sigma (April 2024) recorded TVL surges alongside Solana points programs: Kamino from about $12M in early November 2023 to $48M on 7 December (the JTO airdrop day) and $248M on 26 December, and Zeta from about $1M to $13.3M by 31 December. It cautioned that marketing efforts confound attributing the gains to points mechanics.

Aster (a BNB Chain perps exchange, not Solana) delayed its airdrop to 20 October 2025 after community feedback flagged 'potential data inconsistencies' in some allocations. It said allocations should not fall below the final snapshot RH% recorded in each epoch, would update allocation data, and gave users 48 hours after the update to choose a USDT refund option.

A delegate approval lets an attacker wait. GoPlus says phishing sites run the Delegate authorization through ApproveChecked behind an ordinary-looking interaction, and the attacker may wait until enough users are deceived and balances are large before moving tokens. MadeOnSol makes the same point: the transaction does not immediately drain the wallet. A wallet whose balance did not change at signing time can still carry a live attacker delegate.

Wormhole's filter also used a minimum cumulative transfer value across linked wallets (median about $1,500, lower for early and consistent users), flagged rapid sequential identical-amount transfers, and used Louvain behavioral clustering only alongside other methods. The snapshot was 2024-02-06 and the post is dated 2024-03-11.

A drainer can set itself as delegate on a victim's token account and drain days later, so owners are advised to review delegates periodically (for example on Solscan) and revoke unfamiliar ones, then verify the revoke transaction before signing.

Rev. Rul. 2019-24 is limited to airdrops after a hard fork. In December 2019 an IRS special counsel said the IRS had no position yet on promotional (marketing) airdrops, and a TokenTax guide updated 2026-11-05 still states there is no IRS guidance specifically on airdrop farming. Points-based and campaign airdrops are therefore taxed by extrapolation, not by direct authority.

Tax tools make airdrop income a setting. Koinly has a 'treat airdrops as income?' switch for users in countries where airdrops are income. The open-source Onchain-Accounting app values staking, airdrop and interest income at the fiat rate on the receipt date and carries that value into the asset's cost basis, which matches the US basis rule.

The closest IRS authority for task-based airdrop and points campaigns is Chief Counsel Advice 202035011 (released 2020-08-28). It concludes that convertible virtual currency paid for microtasks on a crowdsourcing platform is consideration for services, taxable as ordinary income and possibly subject to self-employment tax. Its examples include downloading an app and leaving a review, completing quizzes and surveys, and registering accounts. IRS FAQs 57, 58 and 60 say the same for digital assets received for services. No source found applies the memo to a Solana points program, so the fit is by

Since 2025-01-01 digital-asset basis must be tracked wallet by wallet or account by account, not in one universal pool. Rev. Proc. 2024-28 let taxpayers make a reasonable reallocation of unused basis to each wallet or account as of that date. A taxpayer who does not accept the default FIFO rule must identify the units sold no later than the date and time of the sale. For multi-wallet farmers, income from every wallet is combined on one return but basis follows each wallet.

Solana drainers run as sold or affiliate kits: Blowfish (2024-02-09) described Aqua and Vanish as 'scam-as-a-service' toolkits and cited Chainalysis for a drainer-kit community of over 6,000 participants; Mandiant found CLINKSINK affiliates (at least 35 IDs, 42 receiver wallets) feeding a common operator, and noted its source code appears to have leaked.

Chainalysis reported in January 2024 that the largest community devoted to one Solana drainer kit had more than 6,000 members (about 6,200 per its analyst Brian Carter), that essentially one dedicated Solana kit, linked to a single developer, was promoted across channels with documentation often in Russian, and that most kits used in crime are not Solana-specific. Every copy of the figure in the sources reviewed derives from that Chainalysis statement.

Chainalysis counted about 6,200 members in the largest community devoted to one Solana drainer kit (January 2024). It said only one dedicated Solana kit was widely promoted, most kits used in crimes are not Solana-specific, and the kit developers have Russian links. Crypto.news, relaying Blowfish, also reports Russian-language documentation and a community of more than 6,000. Both outlets relay Chainalysis, so the member count is one measurement, not two.

A legitimate domain can also deliver a drain. Decrypt reports that in March 2026 attackers who compromised a Bonk.fun team account pushed a prompt on the bonk.fun domain asking users to sign a fake terms-of-service message, and the team told users not to use the domain. The team said only users who signed after the compromise were affected and disclosed no loss figure.

LayerZero called its public sybil list preliminary: it 'should not be considered definitive until the final report is published, as addresses may be removed from the sybil list as calculations are refined'. It said its first analysis targeted 'industrial sybil clusters' and that it narrowed over two million initial flags to 803,093 to minimise false identifications. Outlets quote the total as about 800,000 or 803,093.

Before signing, look for three instruction types: Approve or ApproveChecked (a wallet may label it 'Delegate'), SetAuthority on an account owner, and System Program Assign. For an approval, check the delegate address, the token account and the amount, and prefer an exact amount to an unlimited one. Revoke approvals you no longer need. After a suspected incident, inspect the confirmed transaction for delegated token accounts, revoke unfamiliar delegates with a trusted tool, and verify the revoke transaction before signing.

Solana Compass offers a free revoker. It reads every token account under the SPL Token and Token-2022 programs, lists the token, delegate, approved amount and whether the amount covers the whole balance, and batches Revoke instructions so most wallets clear in one or two signatures. GoPlus's guide also advises periodic use of 'tools like Solana Revoke'. No audit of any of these revokers turned up.

HMRC's Cryptoassets Manual (CRYPTO21250, updated 2025-11-28) defines an airdrop to include marketing allocations, automatic allocations for holding other tokens, and allocations to people who registered. Airdrops given in return for, or in expectation of, a service are subject to Income Tax as miscellaneous income or trade receipts. Income Tax may not apply if the tokens arrive in a personal capacity with nothing done in return, no link to a service or condition, and no trade or business in exchange tokens or mining. Disposal of an airdropped token may produce a Capital Gains Tax charge in eit

On 2026-08-19 the ATO issued draft Taxation Ruling TR 2026/D1 on the receipt and disposal of crypto assets by an airdrop. It covers issuers and recipients, both in a crypto trading business and on capital account. KPMG reports that the draft says a recipient who is not carrying on a crypto trading business and does not receive the tokens as a reward for services is not taxed on their value, and that the untaxed market value at receipt becomes the first element of the CGT cost base. The Tax Institute's submission says the draft treats unsolicited tokens as received property.

The Tax Institute of Australia (submission published 2026-10-16) objects that TR 2026/D1 treats unsolicited tokens as received property without asking whether the recipient knows about them or can control them. It notes that in Poulton v Conrad (High Court No. H1/2026, judgment reserved) the Commissioner argued that possession requires awareness and an intention to exclude others. It also says the draft was issued six days after that hearing, is proposed to apply retrospectively, and should not be finalised until judgment is delivered.

The IRS has no rule for spam or unsolicited airdrops. Practitioner views are cautious and non-authoritative. TokenTax says the answer depends on whether the holder could actually control the token and whether it had a supportable fair market value, and that many spam tokens have no meaningful market. A CoinLedger CPA writing in CoinDesk (updated 2024-11-12) says that for unsolicited airdrops true receipt may not occur. An Intuit TurboTax community expert said in January 2025 that an unsolicited zero-value NFT airdrop flagged as a scam typically need not be reported.

Tax tools handle spam by exclusion. In Koinly, marking a token as spam deletes all transactions with that token, hides its balances, and applies to future imports. Koinly advises this for tokens that arrived unsolicited, were never touched and are worthless, and says it does not know which options your country allows. The open-source ChainLedger exporter, which supports Solana, writes spam, dust and airdrops to an excluded CSV with a reason for each row. KoinX warns that manipulated liquidity pools can give spam tokens inflated prices that distort reported income if they are not flagged. Exclu

Koinly says a dust attack, in which a scammer sends tiny deposits of a legitimate token such as SOL, should not be marked as spam. It advises tagging the deposits as Airdrop or Reward instead, and aggregating them if they arrive daily. The amounts can be so small that they display as zero.

Vendors and researchers say they favour precision over recall, but none publishes precision measured on independently verified real users. A Chaos Labs author's thread on LayerZero quotes 'Real users should not be hurt; we aim to maximize precision over recall' and says the work with LayerZero and Nansen aimed at 'minimal false positives'. OpenBlock Labs' docs claim a 'negligible false positive rate' and say 'We always prioritize precision', with no numbers. ZKsync says its sybil step 'intentionally used a very conservative heuristics framework'. ARTEMIX says it maximizes precision over recall

In both the SPL Token and Token-2022 programs, Approve writes one delegate and one delegated_amount onto the source token account (an overwrite, so a new Approve replaces the previous delegate), and it must be signed by the account owner.

The RPC method getTokenAccountsByDelegate returns SPL Token accounts whose approved delegate matches a supplied address, filtered by mint or program id. An investigator can use it to list the token accounts that approved a suspect delegate address, with one call per token program (Token and Token-2022).

Legitimate issuers also use PermanentDelegate. Solana's PYUSD page says the Paxos-issued stablecoin is a Token-2022 mint with an active permanent delegate, so the issuer can transfer or burn PYUSD from any account, for example to comply with a legal order. QuickNode's integration guide describes the same purpose. The extension signals who controls a mint and what they can do to your balance. It is not proof of a scam.
SetAuthority with AccountOwner changes a token account's owner and also clears its delegate and delegated_amount, in both programs. The current owner must sign it.

Rev. Rul. 2023-14 (IRB 2023-33) holds that staking rewards are included in gross income in the year the taxpayer gains dominion and control, valued at the date and time control is gained. It applies the same dominion-and-control timing test as Rev. Rul. 2019-24. It does not mention airdrops, and its footnote 3 reserves other rules such as section 83.

Jarrett II (No. 3:24-cv-01209, M.D. Tenn., filed 2024-10-10, tax year 2020) renews the argument that tokens created through staking are new property taxable only on disposal. EY reported in June 2026 that trial was set for 2026-09-29. No outcome was found in this pass. The IRS position is Rev. Rul. 2023-14, and revenue rulings do not bind courts.

In Paschall v. Commissioner, T.C. Memo. 2026-46, the Tax Court held that eToro-credited Cardano staking rewards were gross income in the year credited, not on sale. It rejected the taxpayer's reliance on Jarrett and found dominion and control despite temporary external-transfer limits. The opinion concerns staking and does not mention airdrops.

Jarrett II (No. 3:24-cv-01209, M.D. Tenn., filed 2024-10-10, tax year 2020) renews the argument that tokens created by staking are new property taxable only on disposal. EY says it alleges that the taxpayer personally validated Tezos blocks. EY reported in June 2026 that trial was set for 2026-09-29. Searches on 2026-11-06 found no report of a ruling or trial. Revenue rulings do not bind courts, so a taxpayer win could change the staking rule.

Brokers report digital-asset sales on Form 1099-DA: gross proceeds for transactions from 2025-01-01 and basis for certain transactions from 2026-01-01. The IRS says the final regulations exclude decentralized and non-custodial brokers. An airdrop received in a self-custody Solana wallet therefore usually produces no third-party form. The IRS says digital asset transactions must be reported whether or not they produce a taxable gain or loss. A custodial platform can still issue a form: eToro issued a Form 1099-MISC for the staking rewards in Paschall.

The amount included in income becomes the holder's basis, so a later sale produces a separate capital gain or loss measured from that value. Rev. Rul. 2019-24 (Situation 2: $50 income, $50 basis) and IRS FAQ 107 state the rule. TokenTax and CoinLedger apply it to modern airdrops, using the receipt-date value as cost basis.

Rev. Rul. 2023-14 (IRB 2023-33) applies the same dominion-and-control timing to staking rewards: the fair market value at the date and time the taxpayer gains control is included in gross income for the year control is gained. The ruling text never mentions airdrops, and its footnote 3 reserves other rules such as section 83. It gives no direct rule for airdrops outside hard forks.

Self-custody airdrop income typically arrives with no third-party tax form, but the duty to report is unchanged. The IRS says the final broker rules require Form 1099-DA reporting of gross proceeds from 2025 and of basis for certain transactions from 2026, and do not cover decentralized or non-custodial brokers. IRS FAQ 108 says to report income from all taxable digital-asset transactions regardless of amount or whether a payee statement arrives. A custodial platform can still issue another form: eToro issued a Form 1099-MISC for the staking rewards in Paschall.

Jarrett II (No. 3:24-cv-01209, M.D. Tenn., filed 2024-10-10, tax year 2020) renews the argument that tokens created by staking are new property taxed only on disposal. EY reported in June 2026 that trial was set for 2026-09-29 and that the plaintiff personally bakes Tezos with his own tokens and infrastructure, a different fact pattern from custodial staking. No report of the outcome was found as of 2026-11-06. Revenue rulings do not bind courts.

Pending US legislation addresses staking but, in the sources found, not airdrops. A June 2026 analysis of the updated PARITY Act draft says a new Subchapter W would make a validator's newly created tokens ordinary income at receipt by default, with an election to defer inclusion for up to five successive years, and that the per-transaction de minimis idea was replaced by a Treasury study with interim guidance in 180 days. The analysis does not mention airdrops or forks and treats the bill as not yet enacted. EY (June 2026) says earlier drafts had non-recognition of staking rewards until dispos

Cointelegraph and Coinspeaker (both 4 September 2024) report that a Jupiter community member swapped into a token called 'RED' that had the PermanentDelegate extension, and the tokens were burned about seven seconds later. Both rest on an X thread by Slorg of Jupiter's Core Working Group, and Solscan showed the burn. PeckShield and Beosin, quoted by Cointelegraph, guessed the motive was supply or price manipulation. Cointelegraph adds that Jupiter and RugCheck built indicators for the extension.

In September 2024 a token called RED that carried the PermanentDelegate extension burned buyers' tokens seven seconds after purchase, per Cointelegraph quoting a Jupiter working-group member. Jupiter and RugCheck had added indicators for the extension. The motive explanations in the article are speculation from PeckShield, Beosin and the Jupiter member.

Arbitrum's pipeline flags addresses that transfer funds within a cluster of more than 20 addresses and addresses funded from the same source, and uses Hop's blacklist and its eliminatedSybilAttackers CSV as inputs; the repo page gives no threshold for 'similar activity'.
Under the classic Token program only the token account owner can sign Revoke. Under Token-2022 the current delegate can also sign Revoke on its own delegation.

Who can sign Revoke depends on the program. In the classic SPL Token program only the token account owner can. In Token-2022 the owner or the current delegate can, so a delegate can drop its own delegation. Checked in token main c58d674b and token-2022 main b797a3b9; the Solana docs say the same.

Solana Compass runs a community-run revoke page. It scans the connected wallet's SPL Token and Token-2022 accounts for active delegates, shows the token, delegate address and approved amount, builds one Revoke per delegated account, and batches them into as few transactions as the wallet supports. It charges no service fee beyond the network fee. The page names no supported wallets, gives no audit or open-source statement, and says it is not affiliated with Solana Labs or the Solana Foundation.
The classic Token program accepts Revoke only from the token account owner. Token-2022 accepts it from the owner or from the current delegate, so a delegate can end its own allowance.

On Solana, Allium's 'first funder' analysis tracks the wallet that sends the initial SOL to a fresh wallet and links wallets funded from one origin. Allium says its Solana work with Wormhole, Jito and Jupiter informed the flagged-wallet list it used for Drift. Wormhole separately says Allium helped build its ownership-clustering and source-funding analysis.

Hop's public bounty rules rejected any reporting methodology 'with a non-negligible chance of removing legitimate users', required methodology to be easy to understand, required at least 10 still-eligible addresses per report, and let self-reporters prove ownership by signing the message HOP_SYBIL_REPORT.

Surface-level rules misclassify real users. Allium warns that excluding wallets by deposit size, volume or transaction pattern often removes genuine users, that traders legitimately use several wallets for security so mutual interaction is not proof of sybil, and that small portfolios can be unfairly cut. Wormhole says some legitimate users may have been caught in its filters, particularly during the recent period of high sybil and spam activity, and that rewards were 'subject to change' while it reassessed cohorts. A Jupiter forum participant makes the same point informally: 'Everyone I know

A Jupiter forum poster (2024-10-16) says many in Sanctum's community disagreed with Sanctum's sybil approach and that this 'creates a lot of fuds' at launch. This is one anecdote. Sanctum's own post of 2024-07-16 states the 61,181 count but describes no detection method and no appeal route.

Phantom's help article on revoking token approvals sends Solana users to a third-party tool, the Famous Foxes Revoker (link target reported as https://famousfoxes.com/revoker): connect Phantom and choose 'Revoke all'. The article names no built-in delegate-revoke screen. It says Solana scams often target Associated Token Accounts.

Jarrett I (M.D. Tenn., No. 3:21-cv-00419) never decided whether newly created tokens are income. The court dismissed it as moot on 2022-09-30 after the IRS refunded the tax. The government's concession there was limited to the refund and did not address the merits of the self-created-property argument.

HMRC's Cryptoassets Manual (CRYPTO21250, updated 2025-11-28) says airdrops given in return for, or in expectation of, a service are subject to Income Tax, either as miscellaneous income or as trade receipts. Income Tax will not always apply to airdropped tokens received in a personal capacity. Disposal of an airdropped token may produce a Capital Gains Tax charge either way. The page does not state a base cost.

Australia reportedly splits airdrops: tokens of an established asset are ordinary income at market value on receipt, while initial-allocation airdrops of previously untraded tokens carry no tax on receipt and a nil cost base. This comes only from vendor summaries; the ATO page returned HTTP 403 and was not read.

Jarrett v. United States, No. 3:21-cv-00419 (M.D. Tenn.), never reached the merits. After the government refunded the tax with interest, the district court dismissed the case as moot on 2022-09-30, and the Sixth Circuit affirmed in 2023. The Joint Committee on Taxation likewise states that no final judgment on the merits was made.

Koinly's summary (updated 2026-05-07) says the Canada Revenue Agency does not treat an airdrop as income for an individual who is not in business, so the whole sale price is a capital gain with nil cost. It says Germany's BZSt treats airdrops as lottery-like, not income, with no income tax on a later sale. These are vendor summaries of other jurisdictions' rules and were not checked against the tax authorities' own pages.

Community answers on the Intuit TurboTax forum (2022-02) say an airdrop is not a gift for tax purposes but a marketing incentive that is income. One answer compares it to a promotional blender for opening a bank account, and says a non-taxable gift typically comes from an individual the recipient personally knows. The forum answers are volunteer and staff opinion, not IRS guidance.

HMRC's Cryptoassets Manual (CRYPTO21250, updated 2025-11-28) says airdrops given in return for, or in expectation of, a service are subject to Income Tax, as miscellaneous income or as trade receipts. Income Tax may not apply to tokens received in a personal capacity without doing anything in return and outside a trade or business involving exchange tokens or mining. Disposing of an airdropped token can give a Capital Gains Tax charge either way. Recap and BittyTax read the manual the same way.

On 2026-08-19 the Australian Taxation Office released draft Taxation Ruling TR 2026/D1 on the receipt and disposal of crypto assets by an airdrop, with draft TD 2026/D2 on wrapping. KPMG reports that the draft would not tax a recipient who is not carrying on a crypto-trading business and did not receive the airdrop as a reward for services, and that the untaxed market value at receipt would be the first element of CGT cost base. The Tax Institute's 2026-10-16 submission says the draft would apply before and after finalisation, with a limited exception for initial-allocation airdrops.

Jarrett I never decided whether newly created tokens are income before sale. The Middle District of Tennessee dismissed No. 3:21-cv-00419 as moot on 2022-09-30 after the government refunded the tax and interest. The Sixth Circuit (No. 22-6023) affirmed on mootness in 2023, and the IRS issued Rev. Rul. 2023-14 shortly after oral argument. In Paschall the Tax Court noted that the government's concession was limited to the refund and did not address the self-created-property argument.

Paschall carries limited weight. EY notes it is a memorandum opinion on a fully stipulated record with a pro se taxpayer and no expert testimony, that the court did not rely on IRS administrative guidance and declined to address a Loper Bright challenge, and that taxpayers without dominion and control over staked tokens may reach a different result.

A Solana token account stores one delegate and one delegated amount at a time. Approve and ApproveChecked write both fields, so approving a new delegate replaces the earlier delegate and its allowance. The token account owner signs the approval.

Review delegates on a schedule and after any risky dApp, mint or claim. Revoke ones you do not recognise, and check the revoke transaction in the wallet preview before signing. Solana Mobile's wallet help, GoPlus and MadeOnSol all give this advice.

Jupiter's founder described the 'Bull Checker' Chrome extension on 19 August 2024. It replaced the wallet adapter's signTransaction, sent the unsigned transaction to a remote server that attached a drainer-program call, and beat simulation by adding SOL to the victim account only after the simulation ran. In one example the user 'lost control of his tokenAuthority' to an attacker address. The post does not name the instruction type and does not advise revoking. All details trace to Jupiter's alert; the press repeats it.

The permanent delegate is stored in its own mint extension and has its own SetAuthority type, separate from the mint authority and the freeze authority. A token whose mint and freeze authorities are revoked can still have a permanent delegate, so a safety check that reads only those two authorities misses it. Solana's PYUSD page lists the permanent delegate and the freeze authority as separate powers.

Revoke clears the delegate and sets the delegated amount to 0 on one token account. It has no partial form: to lower an allowance, the owner sends a new Approve. A wallet with many delegated token accounts needs one Revoke instruction per account, and several instructions can share one transaction.

The Solana CLI revokes with spl-token revoke <TOKEN_ACCOUNT_ADDRESS>. The argument is the token account, not the wallet address and not the mint. After a revoke the token account's delegate field should be empty and its delegated amount zero.

Revoke clears the delegate and sets delegated_amount to 0. It has no partial form: to lower an allowance, the owner sends a fresh Approve with the smaller amount. A frozen token account rejects both Approve and Revoke.
The spl-token CLI revokes one token account at a time with 'spl-token revoke <TOKEN_ACCOUNT>'. The address must be the token account, not the wallet address or the mint.

One single-author dev.to post (18 March 2026) says a hidden System Program Assign inside a benign-looking transaction leaves the wallet preview showing no transfers and no approvals, and that a Solana Blink can deliver it. The post cites SlowMist but gives no transaction links, so treat it as unverified. It supports one point only: a preview that lists no approvals does not rule out an owner change.

Phantom, with Lighthouse Protocol, adds on-chain Guard Instructions that check that state changes match the preview and block the transaction if they differ. Phantom's post is undated and does not say whether approvals or authority changes are covered. Jupiter's alert says Blowfish's SafeGuard does similar work and is being adopted by Solana wallets.

Revoke does not help after a key or seed phrase leak. The attacker holds the owner key and can sign Approve, Transfer or SetAuthority at will. Solana Compass advises moving the remaining assets to a brand-new wallet created on a clean device.

Disconnecting a dApp or wallet session does not remove an on-chain approval. The delegate stays active until the owner revokes it or the allowance is spent. Phantom's Connected Apps screen alone does not revoke token permissions.

Disconnecting a dApp or wallet session does not remove an on-chain delegate. The delegate stays active until the owner revokes or replaces it, or the allowance runs out. Phantom, Solana Mobile's wallet help, Solana Compass and MadeOnSol all state this.

Phantom's help article on revoking approvals sends Solana users to a third-party tool: open Famous Fox's Revoker, connect Phantom and select 'Revoke all'. It names no in-wallet delegate screen. MadeOnSol reads it the same way: the article 'describes its Solana approval workflow and links to a revoker'.

Programs can leave stale approvals. An Immunefi report (10 November 2024) on Jito Restaking says the program approves an unlimited token allowance to a delegate account and has no revoke path, so old delegates keep their allowance after the delegate admin changes the delegate. The report page states no status or reward.
Revoke sets the account's delegate to none and delegated_amount to 0. There is no partial revoke; lowering an allowance means a fresh Approve. Frozen accounts reject Revoke.

The token programs have no separate 'unlimited' flag. The allowance is a u64 amount in base units, and an 'unlimited' approval is an Approve with an amount at or above the whole balance. Solana Mobile's wallet help calls unlimited approvals the riskiest kind, and the Solana Compass revoke page shows whether each approved amount covers the whole balance.
Revoke rewrites two fields on an existing account and moves no lamports, so it costs the transaction fee and no rent. Solana Compass states the cost as the standard network fee, a fraction of a cent.

Solflare has a built-in screen for revoking delegates: Settings > Security & Privacy > Spending approvals. Solana Mobile's wallet help (July 2025) and MadeOnSol (updated October 2026) both give this path.

Open question: No source found measures how often Solana thefts use delegate approvals. Scam Sniffer (13 January 2024) says that, unlike Ethereum where most thefts come from malicious approvals, most Solana phishing signatures start direct transfers. The SolPhishHunter text has no Approve, delegate or revoke category. GoPlus (January 2024) documents delegate approvals through ApproveChecked as a technique in use. Revoking delegates therefore covers a real but unquantified share of Solana drain risk.

Open question: No source reviewed publishes an independent false-positive rate for a major airdrop sybil filter. Artemis gives no performance metrics, Arbitrum's repo page describes no appeal or false-positive handling, the arXiv paper reports no label error rate, and The Block's Linea report contains no quote on false positives beyond the appeal provision.
